claims: As of March 2026, Italian citizenship by descent (iure sanguinis) has been restricted.
Applicants must now generally prove a parent or grandparent was born in Italy and held exclusively Italian citizenship at the time of the descendant's birth.
Previously unrestricted ancestry claims are limited.
Existing citizenship is unaffected.
Applications submitted by March 27, 2025, are honored.
The law limits recognition to applicants with a parent or grandparent born in Italy who held solely Italian citizenship at the time of the descendant’s birth (or at their own death if earlier).
If an Italian ancestor naturalized in another country before their child was born, the chain of citizenship is broken.
The previous right of blood (jus sanguinis) allowed unlimited generational claims.
The previous right of blood (jus sanguinis) has been replaced with a strict parent/grandparent requirement.
Italian citizenship by descent (jure sanguinis) requires an uninterrupted line from a parent or grandparent born in Italy who did not naturalize elsewhere before the next generation's birth.
A foreign spouse of an Italian citizen can apply after 3 years of marriage if residing abroad.
A foreign spouse of an Italian citizen can apply after 2 years if living in Italy.
The marriage period is reduced to 1.5 years if there are minor children.
Non-EU citizens can apply after 10 years of legal residency.
EU citizens can apply after 4 years.
Individuals with parents or grandparents born in Italy may apply after 2 years of legal residency.
Birth certificates, marriage certificates, and death certificates for every person in the direct line are required, translated into Italian and legalized (e.g., with an Apostille).
Official proof is required that the Italian-born ancestor did not become a naturalized citizen of their new country before the birth of the next generation.
Applications are generally handled through Italian consulates abroad or directly in Italy through residency.
Children of Italian-born women born before 1948 previously needed to file a lawsuit to claim citizenship.
Women could not transmit citizenship prior to 1948.
New rules allow voluntary acquisition of citizenship for minors if a parent is an Italian citizen by birth and declares intent within a specific timeframe.
